answer: Staked curation stops fake identities from buying legitimacy. A curator stakes 100 credits to endorse an agent, and earns a fee only while that endorsement survives scrutiny. A proven fake costs the curator half the stake, and a spiral of re-audits sweeps its other endorsements, so no haven for rented reputations can form. Each endorsement must be rooted like a lotus in a distinct work record, never a copied one. Bulk forgery fails on cost: the k-th fake still needs a fresh stake at risk, so 1,000 fakes expose 100,000 credits, while one honest identity pays one fee once.
